summary: Umpqua NF lookout in Douglas County, OR: cabin 1912, L-4 cab 1936 on concrete pillars, removed by burning in 1962. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 14x14 foot L-4 cab on six-foot concrete pillars (1936), after a 1912 log house
facts.status_note: L-4 cab removed by burning on site in 1962

staffing.status: named lookouts from 1919 to 1933; no later staffing found

events.note: First lookout house, built of hewn logs and native shakes
Forest planned to use Devil's Knob as one of three principal lookout stations (Roseburg Review, via Weebly)
F.A. McMillan employed as the forestry lookout; first named lookout in these sources
His wife served at the station
Register says a cupola cabin replaced the 1912 cabin in 1922
History page says a cupola was added to the lookout house in 1927
Jake Smith was the lookout in the South Umpqua District
CCC camp letter describes the man in charge locating fires by bearings from a second lookout
Old 1912 house razed in September; new 14x14 L-4 cab on six-foot concrete pillars
Lookout structure removed by burning on site; FireLookout.com says destroyed
Registered December 10, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the cupola cabin that replaced the 1912 cabin to 1922; the Oregon Lookouts history page dates a cupola added to the house to 1927. The story reports both.
The register says removed in 1962, FireLookout.com says destroyed, and the history page says removed by burning on site. These describe the same event.

notes_for_editor: Weebly and the register agree on 1912, 1936 and 1962. The 1936 structure is called a cab on six-foot pillars, not a tower. No source describes the site today or public status. TopoQuest gives a locale at 4,740 ft against the register's 4,820 ft; not used. A 2024 Forest closure near Highway 46 was found in search but nothing ties it to this lookout, so it is not used. Revision 2026-10-09: no source calls Devils Knob a summit, so the story calls it a former lookout site; the register gives the 1962 removal without a method and the story attributes burning only to the history page.
